one_month_reasoning: The only major scheduled event in the window is TI's Q3 2026 report (not yet confirmed in the files I read; TI reported Q3 2025 on Oct 21, 2025, so expect ~Oct 20-27, 2026, inside the window). Q3 guide was $5.65-6.15B revenue / $2.23-2.57 EPS; consensus sits at the midpoint ($2.39), so the print itself is unlikely to surprise much. The swing factor is the Q4 guide: consensus Q4 EPS $2.18 already embeds a seasonal step-down, while management said lead times stretched a couple of weeks and price increases are rolling through Q3-Q4, which argues for upside risk to Q4; against that, the stock is +63% y/y and TI has a habit of guiding conservatively, with 196 inventory days giving it room to meet demand without urgency. Also in window: dividend record date Oct 30 (no price effect) and possible regulatory news on the Silicon Labs close (minor for TXN). I see no strong directional edge, so the 1-month distribution is centred at ~$294.5 (tiny drift) with ~11-12% monthly sigma (42%/3.5) and fatter tails for an earnings reaction of +/-7-10%.

fair_value.method: Blend of 25x (peer median CY27 P/E) on my CY2028 EPS of $11.00 at the horizon = $275 (60%) and a 3.25% FCF yield on ~$9.50/share forward FCF = $292 (40%); blended ~$282.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Horizon (Oct-2027) NTM EPS ~= CY2028 EPS $11.00 x 25.0x

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus CY2028 $11.59 has only 5 estimates; I haircut ~5% for cyclical peak risk (Q2 revenue +23% y/y with industrial +30%, data center 2x, so 2028 sits late in the upcycle) and for Silicon Labs: SLAB's own projections show 2027E/2028E NOPAT of $168M/$260M (source 13) against a $7.5B cash price funded with cash and up to $5B of term debt (source 2), i.e. ~$300M/yr after-tax financing and forgone interest, so the deal is roughly EPS-neutral until the ~$450M synergies (source 7) ramp. Still ~12% above CY2027 consensus, supported by falling capex/depreciation growth and price increases discussed on the Q2 call.

Peer median CY2027 P/E across 11 peers = 25.0x (range 14.6-74.9x; core large-cap analog/MCU subset median 20.9x). TXN trades at 29.9x CY27 today. I use the peer median, not a premium: TXN's next-year EPS growth (+16%) is below every peer's, which offsets its superior gross margin (61%), 300mm cost position and FCF conversion.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: Forward FCF ~$8.7B / ~915M diluted shares = ~$9.50/share; required yield 3.25%

inputs_detail.derivation: Revenue ~$24-25B (TTM $19.45B; Q3 guide midpoint $5.9B annualizes to ~$23.6B; plus high-single-digit growth), CFO ~42% of revenue (TTM 44.6%) = ~$10.3B, less ~$2.2B capex, plus ~$0.5B remaining CHIPS grants (of $1.6B, $630M received per 10-Q), less ~$0.2B after-tax interest on acquisition debt; 920M diluted shares (Q2) trending slightly lower.

Current TTM FCF yield is 2.4% ($6.53B on $268B market cap) while capex is still elevated; as capex normalizes, I require a yield modestly above that to reflect late-cycle earnings and ~4% cost of TI debt.

bear.story: Analog upcycle peaks in H1 2027: customers that rebuilt inventory in 2026 digest it, price increases stick only partially, utilisation falls in the new 300mm fabs (depreciation ~$2.2B/yr is largely fixed). CY28 EPS ~$9 at ~22x (peer core median).

base.story: Recovery continues at a slower pace; CY27 EPS ~$9.8-10, CY28 ~$11; capex falls toward $2B lifting FCF/share to ~$9-10; Silicon Labs closes H1 2027 and is modestly accretive; stock holds a slight premium to the peer median ~26-27x.

bull.story: Pricing plus data-center (2x y/y) and industrial strength push CY28 EPS to $12.5-13; operating leverage on fixed fab costs lifts GM above 65%; market pays ~30x as FCF exceeds $10/share.

comps_summary.peer_range: CY2027 P/E 14.6x (NXPI) to 74.9x (LSCC); core large-cap analog/MCU subset (ADI, MCHP, NXPI, ON, STM, IFX) 14.6-25.0x, median 20.9x. Fwd EV/EBITDA 10.5x-151x (estimated, see note).
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: TXN trades at 29.9x CY2027 consensus ($293.8 / $9.84), ~20% above the 11-peer median and ~43% above the core large-cap subset. Our 25.0x on horizon NTM EPS sits at the peer median, inside the range.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium is applied. TXN has structurally higher gross margin (61% in Q2), an owned 300mm cost base and the cleanest capital-return record (23 straight dividend increases), but its next-year EPS growth (+16%) is the lowest in the set, and its cyclicality is similar to ADI/MCHP/NXPI. Those offset, so the median is used. Note on basis: all P/Es use calendar-2027 consensus EPS (Nasdaq/Zacks yearly and quarterly consensus; Oct, Mar, Jan and Sep fiscal-year companies calendarized as shown in growth_next_yr). Forward EV/EBITDA is an estimate: EV / [TTM EBITDA x (1 + 0.6 x CY27 EPS growth)]; it is distorted for MPWR, ALGM, POWI, LSCC and SMTC by GAAP stock comp and amortization, so I give it no weight in fair value.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$215 (about 22x CY2027 consensus, the large-cap analog peer median, and ~27% below today) the market would be pricing CY27 EPS near $8-8.5, i.e. no growth from 2026. That would most likely mean the 2026 recovery was largely inventory restocking and price increases failed, or the Silicon Labs deal/financing has gone wrong, rather than ordinary 42%-vol noise.

reasoning: Primary-document picture: Q2 2026 revenue $5.46B (+23% y/y, +13% q/q), GM 61%, EPS $2.14 (incl. 5c discrete tax); Q3 guide $5.65-6.15B / $2.23-2.57; TTM FCF $6.53B helped by $1.18B CHIPS grants; capex 2026 $2-3B vs $4.9B a year earlier; inventory 196 days; price increases started mid-Q2; China 22% of revenue (10-Q). Balance sheet: $7.0B cash+ST investments vs $14.1B debt, plus an undrawn $5B 364-day delayed-draw loan for the $7.5B Silicon Labs deal (HSR cleared May 22, SLAB holders approved Apr 30, other approvals pending; close H1 2027). Dividend raised 7% to $6.08/yr. Valuation: on a single calendar-2027 consensus basis the 11-peer median P/E is 25.0x vs TXN at 29.9x; with no persuasive structural premium (lowest EPS growth in the set), 25x on a haircut CY28 EPS of $11 gives $275, and a 3.25% FCF yield gives $292; blended fair value ~$282, ~4% below spot. Momentum/upcycle evidence (lead times, pricing, data center doubling) argues against a large de-rating near term, so I centre the 12-month distribution at ~$292 (median just below spot) rather than at fair value. Spread: annual sigma ~33% core with a 15% fat-tail component at 60% sigma, a bit below the 42% realized vol (which was inflated by the 2025 tariff shock) but reflecting a late-cycle semiconductor. Scenario check: bear $195 (25%), base $295 (50%), bull $390 (25%) gives mean ~$294, and the ladder puts P(<206) at ~17% and P(>=397) at ~20%, consistent with that. Research limits: Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage estimate endpoints were unavailable (plan/rate limit) so consensus came from Nasdaq/Zacks feeds; sec.gov rate-limited one batch of requests.
